card: Updates doc/i2p.md to document that -privatebroadcast creates transient I2P addresses instead of reusing the persistent address in i2p_private_key. It also clarifies that -privatebroadcast applies only to transactions submitted through sendrawtransaction rather than wallet transactions. The change is documentation-only with no functional code changes.
changed_since_previous: Refined the explanation to note that private broadcast also operates over Tor and added co-author attributions.
evidence: PR description: 'It is not entirely accurate that persistent I2P addresses are used for making outbound connections and accepting incoming ones, as the -privatebroadcast option forces the use of a new transient destination for each transaction it relays.'
problem: Bitcoin Core's I2P documentation stated that persistent I2P addresses are always used for outbound and inbound connections, obscuring the privacy mechanism used by -privatebroadcast and leaving operators misinformed about when their long-lived I2P address is exposed.

risk.why: This is a documentation-only update to doc/i2p.md with no executable code changes.

summary: Clarifies in doc/i2p.md that outbound I2P connections opened under -privatebroadcast use transient addresses instead of the node's persistent I2P identity. It also notes that -privatebroadcast only covers transactions broadcast via sendrawtransaction, and mentions that private broadcast runs over Tor as well.
